design.concept: A focused personal-registration screen. A quiet header names the page and shows the access situation as a chip. A left rail says who the person is in the organization (profile card) and where the release request stands (vertical stepper). The right column is the one form that completes only the minimum data, with a single save button at its end.
design.decisions: Single view, so no scene host: the template forbids tabs, wizards and sectioned shells. Hierarchy follows the defs priority: the situation (profile card plus persistent release banner) is read first, the minimum-data form is the main work, and the timeline is a quiet secondary block under the card. On desktop I used a rail (situation) and a main column (form) instead of one long column, so the form stays in view next to who the person is. The form column has a single subject title ('Dados mínimos'), required fields marked up front, and the save button disabled until name and country are filled (plus consent when the backend says it is required). The save label names the outcome; a failure shows above the button in body color and the label becomes a retry, and the typed values stay in the draft. Success is an inline confirmation near the button. When the access is already complete, the form is replaced by a calm note and no save button. The phone field is left out because the shared draft has no phone leaf; phones are shown read-only in the card from the contacts field. Nothing is computed: the chip, banner, consent field and stepper all read backend fields. Loading, empty, selection-invalid, precondition-missing and error states are designed, with retry and a way back.
